newsitem.title: CANADA: Pools seek court challenge to poison pill.
newsitem.headline: Pools seek court challenge to poison pill.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators will challenge United Grain Growers Ltd's massive share dilution plan at a March 11-12 court hearing, MPE lawyer Anders Bruun said.

"We'll be asking the court that it will be necessary to rule on the validity of the (poison) pill as opposed to just assuming it to be valid and making a technical decision on whether it's triggered or not," Bruun said.
UGG filed asked Manitoba's Court of Queen's Bench Tuesday to rule on whether its massive share dilution plan had been triggered when the Pools made its C$172 million takeover bid.
AWP and MPE raised their stake in UGG to 14.98 percent February 13, then made their hostile takeover bid Thursday.
The Pools also said they had an irrevocable lock-up deal with a group of shareholders with 6.4 percent of UGG stock.
UGG's board passed a poison pill February 14 that triggers after an investor has more than 15 percent of UGG stock.
UGG management said Friday the pill was triggered. The Pools said it was not.
"We planned to go to the commissions and court to show the poison pill was just a tool to entrench management," Griffiths McBurney corporate finance managing partner Tom Budd said.

The Pools' irrevocable lock-up deal lead UGG to state the "poison pill" was triggered and will take effect March 4. At that time, each UGG shareholder except the Pools, will have the right to buy up to 8.5 more shares at C$5.88 each.
"They're going to flood the market with 94 million shares," the Pools financial consultant Budd said. "They will ruin their own company by triggering the pill."
UGG shares opened down C$0.15 at C$14.15 Wednesday. The Pools offer Thursday was for C$13.75 a share, after which UGG stock shot up to an all-time high Friday of C$14.50.
